title: Restricted MCP surfaces default-allow newly added tools
wanted_capability: Every registered MCP tool is deliberately classified for each restricted surface. Either restricted surfaces are default-deny for tools not named by their allow set, or a build-time check fails when a tool is added without an explicit per-surface classification. Today the default and agent-internal surfaces are disallow-list only, so each new tool (for example bbox_embed_partitions, which can prune and scrub vector partitions) is visible and callable there without any surface config change, while its sibling bbox_embed_status is explicitly denied.
fallback_used: Used ?surface=interactive for operator calls; no config change made.
evidence: system-defaults/mcp-surfaces/routing.json: default_surface and agent_internal_surface have allow: [] and a disallow list; bbox_embed_status is disallowed, bbox_embed_partitions is not listed
src/server/surface.rs ToolSurfaceVerdict::permits: empty allow returns true for any tool not matched by disallow
src/server/handler.rs call_tool: 'tool not available on surface' refusal only fires for tools the verdict does not permit
No test or lint compares the router tool set against per-surface classification
notes: Triage trace: still relevant at 8ca82233. Routing packet posture unchanged; no classification check exists.
